sssLowVerdict.text: no known particle This combination is colour-neutral, but there is no known particle with these quarks at spin ½. With colour antisymmetric, spatial symmetric, and flavour symmetric (three identical s), the spin wavefunction is forced to be symmetric — only J = 3⁄2 is allowed. Try J = 3⁄2.

uuVerdict.text: no particle 2 quark(s) + 0 antiquark(s) is not a colour singlet — need qqq, antiq-antiq-antiq, or q-antiq. Only qqq, q̄q̄q̄, or q q̄ are colour singlets — the strong force forbids anything else as a free particle.

ccVerdict.text: beyond table The combination is colour-neutral, but this table covers light hadrons (u, d, s) only. The real particle: J/ψ (charmonium, cc̄) — discovered 1974. Creating it needs ≈ 3.1 GeV of collision energy (its rest mass) — heavy quarks are made in accelerators, not built by hand.
